title: Results: zero-shot forecasting models and GB electricity demand (release demand-results)
note: Release of 4 Nov 2026. Preregistered zero-shot test of TimesFM 2.5, Chronos-2 and Timestral-209M on GB national demand a day ahead, 1 Jan 2024 to 31 Oct 2026. Chronos-2 and Timestral beat a weekly-lag regression by about 7% and 9%, neither shown to reach the 10% bar set in advance; TimesFM 2.5 no better. Points to RESULTS.md, tags demand-plan and demand-plan-dev1, and the deviations log.

title: Demand study results note (RESULTS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Primary, 1,035 days, mean daily MAE over the regression's (1,553 MW), 90% intervals: TimesFM 2.5 1.009 (0.978-1.042), Chronos-2 0.928 (0.902-0.955), Timestral 0.910 (0.885-0.935). Six one-sided Holm-adjusted tests: Chronos-2 and Timestral better at all (p below 0.0005); better by 10% not shown (p 0.962 and 0.730). Seasonal naive 2,095 MW; the regression is at 0.741 of it.

title: Demand study results note (RESULTS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Setup: forecast issued 09:30 UK on D-1 from demand up to 08:30, every half-hour of day D, MAE against the initial outturn. Models see eight weeks of demand only, no weather, no calendar. The regression uses demand at D-2 and D-7 plus day-of-week, bank-holiday and Christmas terms. So inputs match on demand history, but the regression alone has the calendar.

title: Demand study results note (RESULTS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Against NESO's published forecast (694 MW, uses weather) each model's error is over twice as large: 2.258, 2.076, 2.035. After each model's release, against the regression: TimesFM 2.5 1.024 (412 days), Chronos-2 0.965 (0.923-1.006; 367 days from 30 Oct 2025), Timestral 1.089 (1.018-1.206; 17 days from 15 Oct 2026, called too few to read).

title: Demand study results note (RESULTS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Checks and caveats: models may have seen GB demand in training; a noise-perturbation check raised no flag, called weak evidence. Rescored on NESO's later series: 1.001, 0.921, 0.904. On bank holidays every model loses to the regression. Chronos-2's lower bound (0.902) is within seed variation of 0.90. An independent recalculation from the saved forecasts reproduced every ratio.

title: Demand study results note (RESULTS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Run record: google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch at 1d952420, amazon/chronos-2 at 29ec3766 (chronos-forecasting 2.3.2, cross-learning off), mistralai/Timestral-209M at 9874d252 (timestral 1.0.0); median forecasts, CPU torch. Official run is attempt 2 on 4 Nov 2026; all sixteen gate checks passed. Moving-block bootstrap over days, blocks of 7, 2,000 draws.

title: Deviations from the preregistered plan (DEVIATIONS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Plan frozen at tag demand-plan, pushed 3 Nov 2026 18:04 UTC. Deviation 1: attempt 1 (3 Nov, after the tag) failed two gate checks, the NESO reconstruction check and a repeatability check; both faults were in the checks. The author saw attempt 1's results, primary ratios included, before fixing them, and recorded a prediction that attempt 2's forecasts would be identical; the note says it held.

title: Deviations from the preregistered plan (DEVIATIONS.md at tag demand-results)
note: Deviation 2: the amendment's lock file and tag reached GitHub after attempt 2 finished (a push failed), so there is no server-side time for the lock before the run. The code attempt 2 ran was pushed before it (commit e02b62f) and its script hashes are in the results. Stated unchanged: plan text, data, weights, model settings, regression, windows, statistics, threshold, primary tests.

title: Preregistered plan, demand study (plan/PLAN.md at tag demand-results)
note: Plan dated 3 Nov 2026, written before any model forecast real GB demand. Primary: six one-sided tests on the full window (better at all; better by 10%, ratio below 0.90), Holm-adjusted at 5%. The 10% bar is a judgement of the smallest gain worth switching for. Result sentences fixed in advance; a power check showed 'not shown to reach 10%' was a likely answer even for a true 10-14% gain.

title: Preregistered plan, demand study (plan/PLAN.md at tag demand-results)
note: Forecasters: three models with an 8-week context (2,688 half-hours), median as point forecast, about 79 half-hours ahead in one call, pinned revisions and weights hashes; licences listed as Apache 2.0 (TimesFM 2.5, Chronos-2) and Mistral's Modified MIT (Timestral). Regression: one least-squares fit per half-hour slot, refit daily on 365 days, lags D-2 and D-7 plus calendar terms.

title: Zero-shot forecasting models and GB electricity demand: a preregistered test (Zenodo record)
note: Zenodo report published 4 Nov 2026, version demand-results, by Andy Moran. Same result statement as the release. The archive is a snapshot of the repository at the tag: plan and lock, amendment, deviation log, code, outputs of both attempts (forecasts, daily errors, results.json), figures and the results note. Only the file listing was read. The record shows no citations.

title: mistralai/Timestral-209M commit history (Hugging Face API)
note: Two commits, both 15 Oct 2026: a squashed initial commit (7394bc1) and a README update (9874d25, the revision the study pins). The listing gives no file names, so the weights are dated to 15 Oct 2026 as the only date the repository has. That is inside our scored window: 3 of the 52 scored weeks start after it.

title: mistralai/Timestral-209M model card
note: Model card: 209M-parameter zero-shot forecaster, one of a family of four sizes; takes past-only and known-future covariates, numeric or categorical; context up to 32,768 steps, 1,024 steps ahead per pass, 21 quantiles; PyTorch on CPU or GPU. Weights under a Modified MIT licence, with a clause against infringing third-party rights; the licence text itself was not fetched. The page shows no date.

title: gb-foundation-model-tests at tag demand-plan
note: From the research call's sources (not fetched separately). Directory listing at the plan tag: the plan folder's last commit is a freeze commit of 3 Nov 2026, and the README at that tag says no model had been run on GB demand and no forecast scored. Consistent with plan-before-results; commit dates are set by the author's machine, and the tag's push time was not inspected here.

title: amazon/chronos-2 model card
note: From the research call's sources (not fetched separately in this run). Card of the study's second model: licence tag apache-2.0, native past-only and known-future covariates, context up to 8,192 steps. The source shows no date for the weights; the study's results note gives 30 Oct 2025 as the release date.

title: mistralai/timestral (inference code repository)
note: From the research call's sources (not fetched). Inference package for the Timestral family, Apache 2.0, running on CPU or GPU. Its README says the weights are not covered by Apache 2.0 and are distributed on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT licence. The licence terms themselves were not in the source.

title: winderai/demand-forecasting-benchmark
note: From the research call's sources (not fetched). A separate benchmark with GB national demand day ahead on 28 days of 2025 and 5 days in Oct 2026: Timestral-209M and Chronos-2 lead a seasonal naive on the 2025 days and are near it on the 5-day window, scored by MASE. Different windows, metric and baseline, no weekly-lag regression: not a replication of the study.

title: you-research (standard): which primary sources support or contradict the claim
note: Standard tier, LinkedIn excluded, 9 sources. It named the release, the repository at the results and plan tags, the three model cards, the TimesFM and Timestral code repositories and the Winder benchmark. Its ratios match the results note. It did not reach the Zenodo record or any weights commit date, and found no direct replication or dispute.

title: you-search: independent replication or dispute of the demand study, 1 to 14 Nov 2026
note: 20 open-web results, LinkedIn excluded. None replicates, cites or disputes the GB demand study. Results were other foundation-model comparisons (Nordic carbon intensity, German prices, a GIFT-Eval explainer) and unrelated load papers. Found nothing.

title: AndyMoran/gb-foundation-model-tests (README)
note: Repository of the study series, MIT licence, Andy Moran (Heaviside Analytics). Repeats the demand study's table (1.009, 0.928, 0.910 with intervals), lists plan, deviations, code, both run attempts and figures, and gives the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23962005. Input data are not in the repository; fetch.py downloads and hash-checks them. A second study adds weather; a prospective column runs.
